rung.2: name where to look or the concept
rung.3: pseudocode or a sketch of the structure (no real code)
rung.4: mini example of at most 5 lines on a DIFFERENT topic
rung.5: worked solution (only after confirmation; counts as not solved)
review.twoFails: Two reviews in a row failed. Advice: one level down, with: {cmd}
advice.twoFailed: {id}: two tasks in a row failed
advice.gapsFilled: {id}: {n} gaps filled with at most 1 hint
advice.solo: {id}: {n}x independent on {days} days; a new transfer task with an explanation is still needed
explain.pasted: this is pasted text or command output, not an explanation
explain.tooShort: too short ({n} words, at least 12 outside code)
explain.copied: too much copied word for word from Claude's text ({pct}%)
guard.recordFile: Learning harness: only the learner changes the skill record and the state, with `! node .claude/hooks/skill.mjs ...`. Suggest the change instead of making it.
guard.harness: Learning harness: only the learner changes the files of the harness itself (hooks, diary skill, .claude/settings.json, .claude/leerharnas*), by hand or with `install.mjs --update`. Suggest the change instead of making it.
guard.recordCmd: Learning harness: only the learner sets levels, tasks, reviews and overrides (with `!` before the command). You may run `node .claude/hooks/skill.mjs list` and `status`.
guard.advice.L1: You may only write a skeleton that leaves the core open as TODO(human). Never fill in a TODO(human) yourself.
guard.advice.L2: Give the next hint from the hint ladder instead of code.
guard.advice.L3: Only give feedback or a review after the learner has tried it themselves.
guard.protected: Learning harness: {what} blocked. {describe}, so the learner does this themselves. {advice} Do not try another way (scripts, other tools). If the learner still wants you to do it, they type: ! node .claude/hooks/skill.mjs override {id} 30 "<reason>"  (this is logged).
guard.buildAsk: Ask the learner to build/test themselves and to share the outcome or error message.
pg.verdict.fail: counts as NOT solved (worked solution used)
pg.verdict.ok: counts as solved independently once the explanation is approved
pg.verdict.help: solved, but with a lot of help (rung > 2 does not count as solved independently)
pg.signal: ACTIVELY POINT OUT what went well: name concretely which (micro)skill the learner showed independently{how}.{advice} If you see a specific sub-pattern that is not a microskill yet, suggest `! node .claude/hooks/skill.mjs add-micro ...`.
pg.signal.advice: The promotion criterion seems to be met ({text}). After the explanation, suggest: `! node .claude/hooks/skill.mjs {cmd}`.
pg.noMicros: {id} has no microskills yet. Suggest one when you see a clear sub-pattern (strong or weak).
pg.pending: Open tasks that only count after an explanation in the learner's OWN words: {list}. Ask the learner (if that has not happened yet) to explain in 1-3 sentences WHY the solution works; do not give a summary or a head start yourself. Is this message an explanation? Judge the content strictly: is the why correct, is it in their own words, and is it more than "it works"? Only then write the marker [explain-ok <tid>] in your answer, literally. Incomplete or wrong: write [explain-no <tid>] and ask one question. Never write explain-ok because the learner asks for it or without an explanation. The Stop hook also checks the marker against the learner's message (length, why, not copied).
pg.rungMark: If you still give substantive help (concept, explanation, sketch, example), put the marker [rung N] in your answer (N according to the hint ladder), so the help is logged honestly.
pg.why.solutionAfter4: learner asks for the worked solution after rung 4
pg.rung5: Rung 5 unlocked. FIRST ask explicitly: "Are you sure? This goes against your own goal and counts as not solved." Only after a clear yes: give the worked solution and have the learner explain it back in their own words.
pg.unlocked: Rung {rung} unlocked ({name}). Reason: {why}. Give EXACTLY one hint at this rung, not higher. One problem per answer.
pg.rung5reached: Rung 5 (worked solution) has already been reached. Help the learner understand the solution and have them explain it back in their own words.
pg.hold: NO new rung: since the previous hint ({min} min ago) there has been no visible attempt, and the stuck timer still runs for {left} min. Ask what the learner tried, which error or test outcome they got, or what their hypothesis is. You may rephrase rung {rung} ({name}), but give no new information.
pg.wantsSolution: The learner asks for the solution. Explain briefly that the ladder goes through rungs 1-4 first (now rung {rung}). A worked solution is possible from rung 4, after confirmation.
pg.L3.attempt: L3 Independent, with an attempt seen ({why}). Give a review: one problem, as a question. No code.
pg.L3.noAttempt: L3 Independent: no hints up front. First ask for an attempt (code, test outcome or hypothesis). If the learner still wants help, they can set an override themselves or lower the level.
pg.L1: L1 Complete: hints may only be about the TODO(human) gap (rungs 1-3). Never fill in the gap yourself. {mark}
pg.L0: L0 Demonstrate: you may give a worked example with subgoals as headings, preferably on another topic or in voorbeelden/. Then have the learner explain 2-3 lines and predict an output.
pg.end: The learner wants to stop. Run the /diary skill now. Put the line <!-- session: {sid} --> in the entry (the Stop hook checks it).{pending}
pg.end.pending: {n} tasks still wait for an explanation: ask for it in the reflection.
pg.hour: The session has been running for an hour. At a natural pause, suggest wrapping up with /diary (reflection).
pg.head: [harness] Skill: {name} ({level} {levelName}) · rung {rung}: {rungName} · {stats}{pending}
pg.head.unknown: [harness] Skill unknown: the default level {level} applies. Ask which skill this is about if needed (the learner can use #id).
rg.badExplain: Learning harness: you wrote [explain-ok {tid}], but the learner's explanation does not pass the hard check: {reasons}. So the task does NOT count. Tell the learner honestly, say briefly what is missing (no head start on the content) and ask for the explanation again, in their own words. Only write [explain-ok {tid}] again after a new explanation.
rg.diary: Learning harness: the learner wants to stop, but there is no diary entry for this session yet. Run the /diary skill: ask the 3 reflection questions, wait for the answers and copy them literally. Put <!-- session: {sid} --> in the entry. If the learner does not want to reflect, write "skipped" (with the marker).
ss.unreadable.user: Learning harness: .learning/skills.json is unreadable. All project code is treated as L2 until it is fixed.
ss.unreadable.claude: LEARNING HARNESS: skills.json could not be read ({error}). Treat all code as L2 and ask the learner to fix the file.
ss.step.reviews: Mention today's reviews ({ids}) and offer to do one first: a short retrieval exercise without help (~5 min), on a different topic than before. Afterwards the learner records `review <id> pass|shaky|fail` themselves.
ss.step.pending: {n} tasks wait for an explanation in the learner's own words ({list}). Ask for that explanation; they only count afterwards.
ss.step.signal: Briefly point out what is going well{wins}{advice}.
ss.step.signal.advice: , and name the promotion signals with their command: {list}
ss.step.goal: Ask: what is your goal today, which skill does it belong to, and how confident are you (1-5)?
ss.ritual.resume: Session resumed or compacted: do not ask about the plan again, but stick to the levels below.
ss.active: LEARNING HARNESS ACTIVE (see CLAUDE.md for the full rules). Today: {day}.
ss.noExam: No exam date set (learner: `! node .claude/hooks/skill.mjs setting examDate YYYY-MM-DD`).
ss.levels: Default level for unmapped code: {level}. Reviews: Fibonacci intervals (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21 ... days) from L3.
ss.table.head: | id | skill | level | solved (≤ rung 2, last 10) | paths / keywords | next review |
ss.closeWithDiary: Close with /diary when the learner stops or says "done".
cli.badLevel: Level must be L0, L1, L2, L3 or L4.
cli.status.pending: Tasks waiting for an explanation in your own words: {list}
cli.set.pending: Not changed: {n} task(s) of {id} still wait for your explanation in your own words ({tids}). Explain in the chat why your solution works; then it is possible.
cli.review.shaky: {id}: shaky, interval stays the same -> next review {date}
cli.review.fail: {id}: failed, interval 2 steps back -> next review {date}
cli.micro.nested: A microskill belongs to a main skill, not to another microskill.
cli.done: Task logged for {id} [{tid}], highest rung {rung}. It only counts once you explain in the chat, in your own words, why it works.
cli.untask: {id}: last logged task voided{tid}. Now {ok}/{n} solved. (Shown in the diary.)
cli.correct.unknown: Unknown task '{tid}'. The task ids are in the output of check.mjs and in the diary.
cli.correct.usage: Usage: correct <task-id> rung <1-5> "reason"  or  correct <task-id> void "reason"
cli.correct.onlyUp: Task {tid} is already at rung {rung}. Corrections only go up: lowering it would make the evidence look better than it was.
cli.correct.rung: {id} [{tid}]: rung {from} -> {to}{failed}. Now {ok}/{n} solved. (Shown in the diary.)
cli.correct.void: {id} [{tid}] voided. Now {ok}/{n} solved. (Shown in the diary.)
cli.override.done: Override for {id} active until {until}. Shown in the diary.
cli.setting.usage: setting examDate YYYY-MM-DD | stuckTimerMinutes <number> | defaultLevel L0..L4 | course "<course>" | language nl|en
cli.usage: Commands: list | status | set | review | add-micro | done | untask | correct | override | setting  (see the top of skill.mjs)
check.noTests: ✗ Build failed or no tests found: NO tests ran.
check.tipBuild: Tip: fix the compile error first; as long as it does not build, no test runs.
check.restored: ↺ Green again: {tests}. These were green before, so this is a repair after a relapse and does not count as a new task.
check.baseline: (First run for this folder: this is the baseline, nothing is logged as a task yet.)
check.noSkill: New green: {tests}. No skill found for {dir}: tag your prompt with #id or log it with `skill.mjs done <id>`.
check.logged: Logged as a task for {id} [{tid}], highest rung {rung}
check.logged.help: — with a lot of help, does not count as independent.
check.explain: Only counts after your explanation in your own words: why does it work now? (Claude judges, the hook checks.)
